tickets.title: Station systems: Run an opt-in station instance with the World clock
tickets.what: Enable an isolated Station systems instance for a World and observe it ticking in its own ImGui window using the existing World time controls.
acceptance: Station systems are disabled by default; enabled Worlds instantiate four independent Lua system objects through sandboxed runtime plumbing without fake Agents or mutable World exposure.
Use SimulationCoordinator and the World facade with existing fixed ticks/time scale; pause freezes station time and reset recreates instances. No rendering-driven or independent station clock.
A separate top-level ImGui window is toggled by menu and toolbar, shows active-World status and elapsed simulation time, and can close without disabling simulation.
Bundled Lua assets use application resource management; multiple Worlds do not share mutable state. Public snapshots/events support deterministic headless verification; no low-level test-only API.

tickets.title: Station systems: Author and persist station starting conditions
tickets.what: Edit the implemented station settings through structured controls and save/reopen a reproducible World scenario rather than live Lua state.
acceptance: Persist authored enablement and implemented settings with backward-compatible World schema defaults; old Worlds remain disabled and no arbitrary Lua table/VM is serialized.
Edits require pause; applying to a started run requires confirmed whole-World reset. Cancellation preserves authored and live state; pause/resume preserves state in memory.
Load/reset reconstruct initial state. Integrate document dirty state, validated edits and history/replay without resurrecting stale Lua instances.

Test round-trips, malformed input, failed writes, legacy loading, reset confirmation and cancellation through existing document/editor seams. Do not add speculative configuration for all later processes.

tickets.title: Station systems: Contain station script failures
tickets.what: See explicit diagnostics and a paused World when model execution fails instead of silently continuing with partially updated station state.
acceptance: Bound Lua execution and memory/resource use using existing scripting safety principles; diagnose exceptions, budget exhaustion and non-finite output.
Stage station tick work and validate before commitment so a failed step neither partially applies state nor advances station time independently of World time.
Physical shortages are valid simulation outcomes and do not trigger software-error pause; headless failure is machine-observable through the existing World seam.
Test failures after an attempted mutation, multiple-World isolation, reset after failure and deterministic successful replay. Keep Agent-behaviour semantics unchanged.

tickets.title: Station systems: Configure and inspect finite resource stores
tickets.what: Author finite starting resources and inspect current quantities separately from their capacities and starting settings.
acceptance: Declare resource identity, units, capacity, starting inventory and qualified/unqualified quantities; invalid or non-finite configuration is rejected before running.
Starting inventory cannot exceed capacity or be negative; current inventory is runtime state, not an authored edit.
Show units, usable versus held inventory, capacity and initial versus current state in the separate window; save configuration and reconstruct on load/reset.
Test zero/empty/full stores, malformed values, isolated Worlds and no runtime dirtying of authored documents.

tickets.title: Station systems: Transfer resources without violating limits
tickets.what: Configure a bounded resource-transfer scenario and observe conserved movement, protected reserves and blocked destinations.
acceptance: Transfers preserve material, cannot overdraw available/qualified inventory or protected reserves, and respect destination capacity. Backpressure never deletes material.
Apply competing transfers in declared deterministic order or deterministic allocation and commit atomically; rejected/partial transfers and unmet requests are visible.
Publish per-store flows and boundary balance residuals with explicit numerical tolerances; material violations pause through the integrated error mechanism, not silent clamping.
Demonstrate two-store transfer and simultaneous competing requests through authored configuration, UI results and World ticks; reset reproduces outcomes.

tickets.title: Station systems: Account for constituent materials in compound resources
tickets.what: Author compound-resource compositions and see their constituent inventory remain conserved across exchanges.
acceptance: Support declared food/biomass/waste compositions, moisture and energy terms where represented; use a documented dry-mass basis for living biomass.
Track nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium separately plus grouped other minerals; bound nutrient nitrogen is not freely interchangeable with atmospheric nitrogen.
Validate composition and conversion balances at declared boundaries, report constituent residuals, and reject impossible configured yields rather than creating material.
Exercise compound transfers and balanced/unbalanced conversion fixtures through World configuration/results; preserve constituent totals under partial transfer and capacity refusal.

tickets.title: Station systems: Schedule resource deliveries
tickets.what: Schedule one-off or recurring resource deliveries and observe accepted supplies, rejected excess and the next arrival.
acceptance: Deliveries add only specified resources at simulation times, respect qualification/store limits and explicitly account for unaccepted quantities without silent overflow.
Define reusable deterministic scenario event ordering, including coincident events, and execute each due occurrence once under accelerated update batching.
Expose schedule editing, next occurrence and delivery outcomes; reset/load restart authored schedules without replay duplication on ordinary pause/resume.
Test empty/full destinations, recurrence boundaries, simultaneous deliveries, zero quantities and World time-scale behaviour.

tickets.title: Station systems: Supply external equipment loads from solar generation
tickets.what: Configure solar capacity and named equipment loads and observe delivered power and unmet demand through illumination/eclipse cycles.
acceptance: External equipment groups declare electrical demand/profile, heat, thermal class, material exchanges, critical floor, priority and allowed curtailment. Establish extensible service-demand and availability contracts without counting internal equipment twice.
Solar production follows configured capacity and illumination; allocated power cannot exceed generation. Zero installed capacity disables a source and unmet critical minima remain explicit.

Do not silently supply missing cooling: distinguish unmet cooling and admit only feasible configured operation. Early electrical demos can use explicitly declared exported energy/heat boundaries rather than hidden infinite sinks.
Show actual/requested service, source output and operating profiles; test conservation, prioritization, eclipse transitions and stable allocation order.

tickets.title: Station systems: Bridge electrical deficits with batteries
tickets.what: Observe finite batteries support loads during an eclipse and recharge when generation permits.
acceptance: Separate nameplate and usable energy; apply state-of-charge/reserve limits and charge/discharge power constraints at consistent boundaries.
Account for charge/discharge efficiency, losses and stored energy; prohibit free energy or reserve double-counting and make reserve policy visible.
Battery demand/output integrates with existing load allocation rather than a second power budget; expose energy, power, reserve and shortfall.
Test exhaustion, saturation, power-limited ride-through, losses, zero capacity and deterministic repeated eclipse cycles.

tickets.title: Station systems: Accumulate heat and reject it through radiators
tickets.what: Observe equipment and cabin thermal reservoirs warm or cool under explicit heat inputs and environment-dependent radiator rejection.
acceptance: Track thermal energy, effective thermal capacity and temperature using stable World-time integration with declared tolerances.

Distinguish temperature-compatible service classes; account for environmental radiation, absorbed heat, emitting temperature and radiator/view assumptions without promising physical distribution modelling.
Route electrical equipment heat once; explicitly account for exported/stored energy and emitted heat rather than treating every electrical input as duplicate local heat.
Expose temperatures, heat flows and limits; test analytic heating/cooling cases, incompatible classes, hot/cold profiles and equivalent update batching.

tickets.title: Station systems: Circulate coolant and provide freeze-protection heating
tickets.what: Observe powered circulation and heating maintain service only while appropriate power and coolant are available.
acceptance: Track finite loop-specific coolant, normal/hazardous segregation and compatible heat-only exchange; coolant is not potable or nutrient water.
Calculate pump/heater demand and resulting heat once, subject to supplied electricity, fluid inventory and equipment limits.
Insufficient coolant or electricity reduces actual circulation/cooling/heating; exposed freeze/temperature limits and unmet service are visible without inventing flow.
Test blackout, coolant loss inputs, heater capacity, isolated inventories and balanced electrical/thermal exchanges through World snapshots.

tickets.title: Station systems: Provide chilled thermal services
tickets.what: Run chillers that supply compatible cold services while consuming real electricity and rejecting condenser heat.
acceptance: Use configured cooling capacity, COP assumptions and temperature interfaces; condenser heat equals extracted heat plus work and applicable auxiliaries at consistent boundaries.
Couple cooling admission with available power, circulation and heat sink. Solve/bound allocation deterministically without a circular assumption of unlimited power or cooling.
Publish cold-side duty, work, condenser heat and unmet demand by class; reject incompatible spare thermal capacity.
Test electricity-limited and sink-limited cooling, zero capacity, temperature incompatibility and transient supply loss without double-counting heat.

tickets.title: Station systems: Ride through cooling deficits with finite thermal buffers
tickets.what: Observe finite thermal storage absorb a cooling deficit, reach its limit and recover when rejection becomes available.
acceptance: Configure sensible or explicitly modelled phase-change buffer capacity, initial energy state and usable temperature limits; stored energy is distinct from instantaneous temperature.
Buffer access requires configured circulation or explicit passive transfer; blackout cannot access a powered-only buffer for free.
Expose available capacity, charging/discharging and exhaustion; recovery consumes real rejection capacity and cannot reset storage instantly.
Test analytic deficit integrals, partly depleted starts, transfer limits, exhaustion and repeated outage/recovery cycles.

tickets.title: Station systems: Generate electricity from finite primary fuel
tickets.what: Run fuelled generators whose output depends on fuel, startup energy and cooling rather than an unlimited power setting.
acceptance: Configure fuel inventory/energy, conversion efficiency, output/ramp limits and startup profile; include fuel consumption and generator waste heat.
Start only with supported startup energy and qualified cooling; zero installed capacity disables the source.
Retain configured shutdown heat and cooling needs after electrical output stops, without claiming reactor physics or nuclear qualification.
Expose startup/running/shutdown states and limits; test failed starts, fuel depletion, cooling loss, ramp limits and full electrical/thermal/fuel balance.

tickets.title: Station systems: Simulate normal and hazardous atmospheres
tickets.what: Observe pressure, composition, humidity and temperature evolve in separately configured normal and hazardous compartments.
acceptance: Configure volume, gas masses, water vapour, temperature and occupancy/load assignment; calculate absolute pressure and partial pressures with documented assumptions.
Account for gas leakage and scheduled airlock losses by mass, including recovered versus lost gas where configured; no unexplained disposal or automatic cross-compartment mixing.
Couple atmospheric thermal state to thermal reservoirs and expose meaningful units and initial versus current conditions; pressure setpoints alone do not prove containment.
Test analytic mixtures, leakage, zero/low inventory, vapour constraints, compartment isolation and deterministic scheduled losses.

tickets.title: Station systems: Consume crew supplies and produce balanced metabolic returns
tickets.what: Configure crew population/activity and observe finite supplies turn into explicitly balanced metabolic returns and unmet demand.
acceptance: Account for food/water/oxygen consumption, CO2, moisture, urine/organic waste and metabolic heat with declared compositions and coefficients.
Under partial supply, distinguish requested from actual consumption; do not generate nominal waste from absent material. Document simplified starvation accounting without inventing physiology.
Keep crew inputs independent of Agents, movement, health, death and behaviour. Retain outputs in appropriate finite stores/compartments, never discard them silently.
Show demand and actual exchanges; test nominal and missing food/water/oxygen cases, nutrient/element conservation and no Agent mutation.

tickets.title: Station systems: Recover and qualify water
tickets.what: Process initially supplied wastewater or condensate into usable water with finite capacity, treatment costs and explicit quality holds.
acceptance: Model collection and condensation with compatible cooling and latent heat routing; do not add latent duty twice to the same energy boundary.
Treatment consumes configured electricity/consumables and respects throughput, source inventory and destination capacities; retained concentrates remain accounted for pending disposal capability.
Distinguish raw, treated, held and accepted potable/process inventory; insufficient quality evidence blocks release and hazardous input remains segregated.
Expose recovery ratio with boundary/interval, retained inventory and costs; test limited cooling/power, exhaustion, full destinations and quality failures. This slice can run without crew processing.

tickets.title: Station systems: Store and eject terminal waste
tickets.what: Store normal and hazardous terminal waste separately and remove only eligible material on a configured schedule.
acceptance: Waste stores have finite capacity and treatment/disposal-ready states; full destinations refuse/backpressure inflow rather than delete material.
Eject only available eligible quantities at scheduled times; record ejected material as external loss and preserve held/untreated waste.
Retain recovered resources in appropriate stores until capacity is reached; not-immediately-needed material is not automatically terminal waste.
Test coincident deliveries/ejection, recurrence, empty/full stores and held waste. Ejection is a scenario input, not a simulated safe trajectory or navigation certification.

tickets.title: Station systems: Produce oxygen and manage captured CO2
tickets.what: Operate electrolysis and finite CO2 capture against actual water, power, cooling and storage availability.
acceptance: Electrolysis has balanced water consumption and oxygen/hydrogen products with finite throughput and explicit heat/chemical-energy accounting.
Supply atmosphere or qualified gas stores through bounded transfers; protect life-support reserves and retain or constrain excess products rather than delete them.
CO2 removal/capture uses finite capacity and applicable regeneration/consumable demand; captured gas is inventory, not vanished carbon.
Expose actual production/capture and unmet atmospheric service; test exhausted inputs, product saturation, unavailable power/cooling and reaction balances.

tickets.title: Station systems: Recover carbon through Sabatier and methane processing
tickets.what: Convert captured carbon dioxide and hydrogen into recovered water and carbon through explicitly balanced reaction stages.
acceptance: Track Sabatier CO2/H2 inputs and methane/water products; methane processing returns hydrogen and produces solid carbon with declared capacity/energy/thermal costs.
Combined processing retains net hydrogen demand; recycled hydrogen never becomes free continuing reactant supply.
Water enters appropriate treatment; carbon goes to configured useful store or terminal waste when surplus. Blocked product destinations constrain throughput.
Show per-stage flows and net resource balance; test reactant exhaustion, full destinations, disabled stages and integrated stoichiometry.

tickets.title: Station systems: Run fuel-cell backup from dedicated reactant stores
tickets.what: Generate backup electricity from finite dedicated hydrogen and oxygen while preserving life-support resources.
acceptance: Configure independent reactant starting stores and source capacity/efficiency; electricity, water, heat and consumed reactants balance.
Allow controlled surplus transfers from ECLSS only after protected breathing oxygen and process requirements; never draw protected oxygen implicitly.
Send product water through treatment and require cooling; integrate battery/load service so backup is limited by usable reactants and electrical ratings.
Test exhaustion, reserve-transfer refusal, blocked water destination and electrolysis/fuel-cell cycle losses; expose backup endurance and actual output.

tickets.title: Station systems: Recover nutrients from organic waste
tickets.what: Use a healthy finite-capacity microbial processor to recover nutrients and water from human/organic waste.
acceptance: Declare feedstock compositions and processing yields with separate nutrient N/P/K and grouped minerals; atmospheric N2 cannot substitute without a configured process.
Account for required oxygen, CO2, electricity, heat, water, consumables and unrecoverable residue; no cost-free nutrient conversion.
Recover into finite qualified stores, route only surplus/residue to waste and propagate backpressure from saturated destinations.
Expose processed mass/recovery and limiting inputs; test elemental balance, finite throughput, absent feedstock and power/temperature eligibility without dynamic condition modelling yet.

tickets.title: Station systems: Degrade and restore microbial processing
tickets.what: Observe microbial capacity change with adverse conditions and recover only through declared time/resources or replacement stock.
acceptance: Track aggregate processor condition from configured starvation, temperature and consumable-exhaustion rules; mark biological coefficients as provisional assumptions.
Condition constrains actual processing and cannot create or delete feedstock, microbial material or stored nutrients without accounted exchanges.
Recovery is bounded and may require configured biological stock/resources; do not instantly restore capacity or simulate individual organisms.
Show condition, limiting cause and restoration progress; test adversity/recovery cycles and continued conservation through reduced performance.

tickets.title: Station systems: Grow and respire a resource-limited crop population
tickets.what: Grow a crop population from configured living biomass using real light, gas, water, nutrients and compatible temperatures.
acceptance: Separate dry living biomass from growing area/capacity and stored food; use declared composition and clearly labelled biological assumptions.
Growth is limited by actual delivered light/power, CO2, water, each tracked nutrient and temperature; account for respiration, oxygen exchange, moisture and heat.
Maintain finite growing capacity and essential circulation dependencies; no free photosynthesis during darkness or missing inputs. Harvest is deferred and growth stops at capacity.

Expose growth/respiration and limiting resources; test darkness, single-nutrient depletion, capacity saturation and material/energy accounting using starting nutrient supplies without requiring microbial recycling.

tickets.title: Station systems: Harvest crops and account for biological losses
tickets.what: Harvest food and recoverable biomass and observe living biomass decline under explicitly modelled adverse conditions.
acceptance: Configure harvest timing/rules and edible/non-edible yield; remove actual living material and preserve its declared constituents into food and waste stores.
Account for adverse-condition biomass loss and returned gases/waste/water using explicit balanced assumptions, not silent deletion.
Full food/waste destinations constrain harvest or route explicit surplus through eligible waste paths; recovery cannot recreate lost biomass for free.
Show harvests, food production, waste and losses; test simultaneous harvest/growth events, starvation/death rules and coupled crew consumption.

tickets.title: Station systems: Grow and harvest algae
tickets.what: Run a separate algae culture using the established biological lifecycle with its own installation limits and harvest allocation.
acceptance: Keep algae biomass, culture volume, capacity, coefficients and condition independent of crops, while reusing safe shared lifecycle/accounting behaviour.
Track culture circulation, light, gas, nutrient and temperature demands; partition harvested biomass into declared food/recovery/waste destinations conservatively.
No shared mutable population state, unlimited output at zero capacity or free production during shortages.
Expose both populations distinctly and test independent starvation, culture capacity, harvesting and combined resource competition.

tickets.title: Station systems: Enforce hazardous treatment and containment boundaries
tickets.what: Operate isolated hazardous processing and reserves with qualified recovery transfers and explicit quarantine.
acceptance: Use separate atmosphere/water/coolant inventories and protected hazardous reserves; heat-only interfaces never transfer coolant/material.
Distinguish filtration, treatment evidence and release clearance. Unknown/failed clearance holds material; generic recovery commands cannot bypass the hold.
Qualified treated transfers respect destination capacity; disposal-ready hazardous waste remains segregated. Pressure targets alone do not establish containment.
Expose independent reserves, holds and unmet containment demand; test accidental-cross-transfer refusal, cleared recovery, full waste stores and heat exchange without mass mixing.

tickets.title: Station systems: Schedule outages and capacity reductions
tickets.what: Schedule deterministic outages for registered installations and observe constrained service and explicit restoration events.
acceptance: Use stable installation identities and shared availability contracts that later generators/processors can register with, not hard-coded special cases.
One-off/recurring capacity changes respect World time and deterministic event order; restore declared availability without replenishing fuel, consumables, buffers or biomass.
Availability loss changes actual admitted operation and relevant power/heat/material flows; no output continues from an unavailable process.
Expose schedule/state and events; test power/circulation loss, overlapping changes, reset/replay and accelerated timing.

tickets.title: Station systems: Perform resource-constrained maintenance
tickets.what: Schedule timed maintenance whose completion requires declared tools, spare parts and consumables.
acceptance: Declare prerequisites, duration and explicit inventory requirements; reusable tools are not consumed unless configured as consumables, and absent prerequisites prevent free completion.
Define deterministic reservation/consumption and interruption rules so overlapping work cannot double-spend parts or tools.
Isolate/update affected installation availability and account for removed parts/used materials into appropriate waste; restoration does not replenish supplies for free.
Expose progress and blocking reasons; test missing tools/parts, interruption, simultaneous jobs, actual resource use and post-maintenance restoration without Agent assignments.

tickets.title: Station systems: Dispatch generation and protect electrical reserves
tickets.what: Automatically bridge source losses, start available backup and allocate electrical service while protecting declared reserves.
acceptance: Coordinate batteries, thermal sources, solar and fuel cells using actual startup/ramp, fuel, cooling and power limits; no sustained supply fabricated by dispatch.
Honor load priorities/critical floors and protected reserves; publish any unmet critical demand rather than relabel it optional.
Expose operating modes and alarms and record dispatch/curtailment actions; physical model errors remain separate from operational shortages.
Test source trips, backup unavailability, exhausted reserves and ordinary curtailment through integrated World scenarios.

tickets.title: Station systems: Protect cross-system service dependencies
tickets.what: Admit or curtail operations without cutting essential support services for protected loads.
acceptance: Resolve declared power/cooling/material dependencies conservatively; admission requires compatible actual services and protected reserves, not independent nameplate totals.
Protect containment, biological circulation, critical sensing/control demand where modelled and shutdown cooling even when related experiments/lights/generation output stop.
Handle competing dependencies deterministically without circular free supply; expose reasons and unmet critical minima.
Test lighting curtailment with preserved circulation, hazardous shortages, generator cooling shortfall and microbial loss under coordinated operation.

tickets.title: Station systems: Recover services without oscillation or overload
tickets.what: Restore equipment and reserves in safe stages after a shortage clears.
acceptance: Establish qualified cooling/protection and source startup prerequisites before restoring heat-producing loads; account for surge/startup demand where configured.
Use declared hysteresis, dwell and restoration rules to prevent rapid shedding/reconnection oscillation; replenish reserves without overloading services.
Recovery actions remain bounded by actual resources and do not bypass quality holds, containment or physical limits.
Show recovery stage/actions and test fluctuating capacity, partially depleted buffers/stores, repeated incidents and failed restart prerequisites.

tickets.title: Station systems: Show bounded trends and incident history
tickets.what: Inspect station resource/service trends and a chronological incident/event history in the separate window.
acceptance: Bound storage for trends/events with explicit retention/downsampling behaviour under accelerated World time; no unbounded per-tick history.
Show units, simulation timestamps, actual versus requested values and subsystem identity; support event types from later features through a stable presentation contract.
Visibility/plotting and UI update frequency cannot mutate state or change simulated results. Indicate gaps/retention limits rather than implying complete history.
Test long runs, toggling window visibility, active-World switches and distinct editor contexts without state leaks.

tickets.title: Station systems: Explain current resource endurance
tickets.what: See conditional endurance estimates from usable inventory and observed net depletion together with reserves and next deliveries.
acceptance: Distinguish physical total, usable/qualified inventory and protected reserve; use explicit current-rate/static assumptions and declared observation interval.
Report unstable/unknown or bounded estimates for near-zero, changing or uncertain net rates instead of unjustified infinite endurance.
Show per-resource constraints and next-delivery context without claiming a universal survival countdown or forecasting future profiles yet.
Test depletion, net production, zero demand, sudden rate changes, unavailable inventory and battery energy/power distinctions.

tickets.title: Station systems: Forecast scheduled resource balance and resupply needs
tickets.what: Project inventory and shortfalls under declared load/resupply scenarios and explain the replenishment needed.
acceptance: Extend static estimates to configured demand/production profiles and future deliveries using explicitly bounded model assumptions; account for store capacities and accepted delivery quantities.
Publish projected inventory at resupply, resource shortfalls and limiting services with scenario/uncertainty labels; do not present uncertain biology as guaranteed recovery.
Forecasting must not mutate live inventories, advance the real World, consume deterministic streams or become an unbounded computation.
Test known analytic profile/delivery cases, delayed resupply, changing service availability and conservation of projected exchanges; document approximation limits.

tickets.title: Station systems: Expose microbial and carbon-loop effects in coordinated operation
tickets.what: Demonstrate recycling changes propagating through gases, nutrient supply, biology, power allocation and alarms.
acceptance: Run coupled World scenarios combining carbon recovery, microbial processing, crops/algae, crew demand and supervision rather than separate standalone fixtures.
Reduced recovery changes actual dependent resources/services; include non-human CO2 sources and net Sabatier hydrogen need without duplicate accounting.
Resolve demonstrated integration defects and surface limiting processes/actions in subsystem views and alarms; retain normal/hazardous segregation and finite waste backpressure.
Test closed-accounting nominal operation, processor loss and recovery, nutrient-limited growth and carbon-stage constraints with deterministic outcomes.

tickets.title: Station systems: Ship one reconciled reference station
tickets.what: Load one packaged editable reference configuration that demonstrates the implemented system with internally consistent budgets.
acceptance: Reconcile one equipment/resource register, source/load/thermal budgets and starting inventories; do not sum incompatible source-spec examples or duplicate growth/auxiliary/reserve margins.

Record coefficient provenance, units and provisional biological/process/thermal assumptions. Explicitly address water makeup/recovery, hazardous autonomy, hydrogen/carbon balance and microbial participation.
Package the configuration through application resources and show assumptions/limits in editor context; accept intentional operational shortages while rejecting physically inconsistent inputs.
Demonstrate a reproducible normal-operation scenario with accounting summaries and documented scope/qualification limits.

tickets.title: Station systems: Ship reference emergency and recovery scenarios
tickets.what: Select reproducible reference scenarios showing delayed resupply, failures, maintenance and recovery with expected visible outcomes.
acceptance: Provide authored variants for resupply delay, power/cooling outages, constrained waste storage/ejection and maintenance/recovery, using implemented mechanisms rather than scripted hidden resources.
Document expected limiting services, key event ordering and bounded outcome ranges with provisional assumptions; traces show why outcomes occur.
Verify pause/reset/load and closing the results window preserve lifecycle semantics; scenario results use existing World and editor seams.
Do not certify safe disposal trajectories, hardware redundancy, human safety or indefinite self-sufficiency from conceptual examples.

tickets.title: Station systems: Demonstrate long-duration stability and repeatability
tickets.what: Run the reference station over long simulated durations without numerical drift, hidden resource creation or unbounded retained history.
acceptance: Define reproducible long-duration workloads and declared material/energy residual tolerances, tracking finite values, inventory bounds and scheduling correctness.
Check bounded runtime/history memory and equivalent outcomes across supported World update batching/time-scale paths, including reset and multi-World isolation.
Fix demonstrated stability defects without masking them with silent clamping or relaxing conservation to hide errors; report performance/assumption limitations.
Use public snapshots/events/diagnostics and existing headless infrastructure; these are model regressions, not flight or engineering qualification.
